CSCO.rationale: Cisco's fundamental trajectory is genuinely positive — revenue accelerating +9.7% YoY to $15.35B, EPS +31.1% YoY, operating margin expanding from 22.2% to 24.6%, and a clean balance sheet (D/E 0.515). The AI infrastructure opportunity ($1.9B hyperscaler orders, ~$4B AI revenue target) and raised guidance (FY2026 EPS $4.27-$4.29) are real. However, the stock has re-rated far beyond what fundamentals justify. PE has expanded from ~28x in March 2026 to 43x currently (95th percentile of 365-day range), while net margin only moved from 17.6% to 18.8% — a 54% multiple expansion against modest margin improvement. Price surged +52.3% in one quarter ($78.51 to $119.54) versus 9.7% revenue growth. Operating cash flow is deteriorating (-18.7% YoY to $1.82B) even as net income grows +31%, raising earnings quality concerns. The 2.3% earnings yield sits 216bp below the 10-year Treasury at 4.46% — no margin of safety. RPO growth at 5% lags total revenue growth of 10% by 500bp, indicating the software transition is not yet converting hardware demand into durable recurring revenue. Security segment revenue declined 4% YoY. Insider selling is persistent (47 sales, zero purchases over 6 months). A reversion from 43x toward the 12-month median of ~29x would imply ~32% downside. The market has priced in near-perfect execution on an incomplete transition.
